item.title: 2027: Northern power brokers, Emirs, Imams behind Tinubu, Yari assures
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Director General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the power brokers of Northern Nigeria, traditional rulers and Islamic clerics are solidly behind his return to office in 2027. He spoke at the flag-off of the party’s presidential campaign in Kaduna, in the presence of the President and all the governors of Northern Nigeria. “We have been engaging all and sundry, our traditional rulers, our ulama and our imams, to understand the importance of your return in 2027 for continuity, for the peace of this country and for Nigeria,” Yari said. He told the President that the northern establishment had turned out in full. “We believe in you, and those people believe in us. All the shakers and movers of this part of the country are here. In the northern part of the country, anybody who is not here today, Mr President, then there is nobody there. We are here. “By God’s grace, Your Excellency, Mr President, we resolve, by God’s grace, that as far as Northern Nigeria is concerned, Mr President, I need your ears. Mr President, I want you to listen to us carefully. Northern Nigeria is 101 per cent for you, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, by God’s grace, Insha Allah. And the promise we have made, you are going to see it on January 16, 2027,” Yari said. Yari described Kaduna as “the spiritual centre of politics in Northern Nigeria”, adding that the venue had drawn “all the governors of Northern Nigeria”. On the economy, he said the President’s reforms had changed the country’s fortunes. “If we talk about the economy, we know the state of the economy when you stepped into the leadership of this country. Today, the total indices have changed completely to the advantage of Nigeria and other countries of the world. “Mr President, I can enumerate at least a few: from the exchange rate, to the subsidy removal and many more,” Yari added. The APC-PCC boss said the party would take its case to voters on the strength of the administration’s achievements. “We Nigerians, at the head of this campaign, are going to campaign with our records. Our records are there. The infrastructure is there. What you did in health, education and human capital development is there. The students are there. The transparent cash and conditional cash transfers are also there for men and women,” he said. Turning to the 2023 election, Yari said: “I would like to be a student again, to be told how you did it, because we want the country.” He said the party was committed to justice and urged the President to listen closely to the North’s message. item.title: Nigeria, South Korea seek stronger trade, technology partnerships
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Nigeria and South Korea have called for stronger bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, technology transfer, agriculture and skills development to promote economic growth and create opportunities for their citizens. The two countries renewed the call at a reception to mark South Korea’s National Day in Abuja on Friday, with both sides expressing commitment to expanding their longstanding diplomatic relations. Speaking at the event, South Korea’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Jeong Yoan, said the two countries, which established diplomatic relations in 1980, had opportunities to deepen economic cooperation through partnerships that support local businesses, entrepreneurship and human capital development. He recalled that South Korea’s economy was devastated by the Korean War, with its annual per capita income below $100 in 1953, but said investment in education, hard work and international cooperation had helped the country rebuild. The ambassador said the theme of the celebration, “One Heaven. One Earth. One Humanity,” reflected the importance of peace, human dignity, mutual respect and international cooperation. He explained that South Korea’s National Foundation Day, known as Gaecheonjeol, is celebrated on October 3 and commemorates the country’s traditional founding story associated with Dangun and the principle of Hongik Ingan, commonly interpreted as “to benefit all humanity.” In her remarks, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, represented by the Chief of Protocol of the Ministry, Ambassador Babagana Wakil, commended South Korea’s achievements in technology, engineering, manufacturing and social development. item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima has appealed to voters in northern Nigeria to back President Bola Tinubu for a second term in 2027, arguing that the President has earned the region’s support through his past backing of northern political leaders. Shettima made the appeal on Saturday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna, where he urged voters to support the party’s candidates across all levels of government. “We have come to ask you to renew a second time for the APC from top to bottom,” he said. The Vice President cited Tinubu’s support for northern figures, including former President Muhammadu Buhari, as a reason for voters in the region to reciprocate by supporting his re-election bid. Atiku said Nigerians were more concerned about the government’s record than its attempts to shift responsibility, insisting that the 2027 presidential election would put Tinubu’s handling of the economy and security under scrutiny. In a statement on Saturday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku accused the President of blaming his political opponents for hardship that had worsened under his watch. “Mr President, blaming the opposition for hunger is either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia. The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record,” Atiku said. item.title: Spurs Seal Rare Win At Chelsea As Palmer Sees Red
item.description: Tottenham clinched a Premier League win at Chelsea for just the second time in 36 years as a woeful own goal from Blues keeper Mike Penders was followed by Cole Palmer’s red card in Saturday’s 2-0 victory. Roberto De Zerbi’s side clinched their second successive league win thanks to Penders’s howler in the second half at a rain-lashed Stamford Bridge. Chelsea forward Palmer was sent off for a second booking moments later before Mathys Tel produced a superb solo effort to condemn the Blues to their first home defeat against Tottenham since 2018. Since 1990, Tottenham had won just once in 41 previous away matches against London rivals Chelsea in all competitions. Ending that miserable run gave Tottenham only their second win in their last 16 league games against Chelsea, both home and away, and their first since 2023. Tarzoor, who spoke with newsmen in Makurdi, described some of Chief Ortom’s comments during a recent television programme as inappropriate, arguing that political differences should not undermine the dignity of the office of the governor or the people of the state. item.title: ADC mocks APC over ‘rented crowds, empty seats’ at Kaduna rally
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, has mocked the All Progressives Congress, APC, over what it described as a disappointing Northwest zonal flag-off rally in Kaduna, alleging that rented crowds and empty seats exposed the ruling party’s declining public acceptance. The council said the rally, which was intended to showcase the APC’s political strength across the Northwest, fell short of expectations despite alleged mobilisation of attendees from the seven states in the zone and beyond. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC alleged that attendees were reportedly paid between ₦50,000 and ₦100,000 each, yet the Kaduna Township Stadium, which it put at a capacity of 5,000, remained sparsely occupied. “For a rally billed as the Northwest zonal flag-off, what we witnessed was a shameful spectacle. Despite the alleged mobilisation of crowds from across the zone and beyond, the stadium remained scantily filled, with empty seats everywhere,” Ologbondiyan said. He also faulted the reception given to speeches by APC leaders, describing it as unenthusiastic and at odds with the ruling party’s attempt to project political strength in the region. The ADC-PCC further questioned President Bola Tinubu’s performance claims, criticising his reported commissioning of road projects at the rally. Ologbondiyan alleged that some attendees expressed dissatisfaction with the APC after leaving the stadium, chanting “Ba mu yi,” a Hausa expression he interpreted as a rejection of the ruling party and its policies. “You can rent a crowd, but you cannot rent acceptance. Even if people attend a rally, that does not mean they have surrendered their convictions. The real test of public support is what Nigerians will decide at the ballot box,” he said. The council accused the APC of recycling promises made during the 2015, 2019 and 2023 election cycles without adequately accounting for its years in power. It also accused Tinubu of shifting responsibility for Nigerians’ economic hardship to opposition leaders instead of addressing the consequences of his administration’s policies, particularly fuel subsidy removal, which it said had intensified the pressure on households struggling with rising living costs. The ADC-PCC urged the ruling party to abandon what it called wasteful political jamborees, apologise to Nigerians over the prevailing economic difficulties and prepare for an orderly transfer of power in 2027. The council maintained that the ADC offered a credible alternative to the APC, expressing confidence that voters would use the next general election to reject the ruling party. “The message from Kaduna is loud and clear: Nigerians are saying ‘Ba mu yi’ to the APC and Tinubu. item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has described the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC, Peter Obi, as a stingy man who is unfit to govern Nigeria. Wike, who spoke at a town hall interactive meeting with stakeholders in Bonny Local Government, Rivers State, mocked the former Anambra State governor’s habit of carrying his own bags. “As a former governor, you cannot be stingy not to have employed a personal assistant who will carry your bag. You want to show you carry your bag. We don’t want such a stingy person as a president,” he said. He called Obi a social media presidential contender, arguing that popularity online was no substitute for the experience and capacity required to govern the country. “Truly speaking, I gave him president of social media. If you were to vote who will be president of social media, I will vote for him. But if it is to govern Nigeria, it is capital no!” Wike said. The minister questioned Obi’s record as Anambra governor, saying the performance of the incumbent, Chukwuma Soludo, should inform public assessment of the former governor’s administration. The party’s governorship candidate, Ocho Obodoeze, made the call after receiving an award from the Correspondents Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Enugu State Council. Obodoeze accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of suppressing opposition parties and urged the state government to allow all political parties to campaign freely in accordance with the law. item.title: EPL: Arsenal see off Everton, go joint-top after Man City defeat
item.description: Manchester City’s flawless start to the Premier League season was ended in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday that allowed Arsenal to join them at the top of the table with victory over Everton. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. Nicolas Jackson struck twice for Unai Emery’s men to continue a fine run of form for a new-look Villa side. Erling Haaland briefly levelled early in the second half, but Maresca was left to rue City not making more of their dominance for large spells of the game. “We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box,” said Maresca. The Villa side that won the Europa League last season was decimated by high-profile departures during the transfer window. But Emery has quickly moulded his new squad into shape with Jackson proving his critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea wrong. The Senegal international pounced on an error by Marc Guehi to fire Villa ahead after just six minutes. Another of Villa’s new signings Zion Suzuki then thwarted City with a string of stunning saves. Haaland headed in his 13th goal in 10 games this season to equalise. Villa, though, swiftly responded as Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to keep out Jackson’s low shot on the hour mark. “A fantastic day to share with our supporters in Villa Park,” said Emery. “We felt that this is our fortress and the energy the supporters gave us was really fantastic.” – Arsenal’s set-piece prowess – Arsenal took advantage to move alongside City on 21 points from eight games with a routine 2-0 win against Everton. Shorn of the creative inspiration of Bukayo Saka, who is set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a thigh injury, Arsenal had to rely on their set-piece prowess to get the job done. Ezri Konsa bundled in his first goal for the club after Everton failed to clear a corner to open the scoring on seven minutes. Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the lead for Mikel Arteta’s men midway through the second period. Fulham further eased the pressure on manager Alvaro Arbeloa with a 1-0 win at Coventry thanks to Oscar Bobb’s individual effort. A second consecutive victory propels the Cottagers out of the relegation zone and up to 12th. Tottenham are also seeking to escape the bottom three when they travel to Chelsea in the evening kick-off, aiming to improve on a terrible record at Stamford Bridge. On Sunday the focus turns on Manchester United boss Michael Carrick when his side take on Bournemouth. A seven-game winless streak has plunged Carrick’s future into doubt just months after he was hired on a two-year deal after a successful interim spell in charge at the end of last season. item.content:encoded: Manchester City’s flawless start to the Premier League season was ended in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday that allowed Arsenal to join them at the top of the table with victory over Everton. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. Nicolas Jackson struck twice for Unai Emery’s men to continue a fine run of form for a new-look Villa side. Erling Haaland briefly levelled early in the second half, but Maresca was left to rue City not making more of their dominance for large spells of the game. “We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box,” said Maresca. The Villa side that won the Europa League last season was decimated by high-profile departures during the transfer window. But Emery has quickly moulded his new squad into shape with Jackson proving his critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea wrong. The Senegal international pounced on an error by Marc Guehi to fire Villa ahead after just six minutes. Another of Villa’s new signings Zion Suzuki then thwarted City with a string of stunning saves. Haaland headed in his 13th goal in 10 games this season to equalise. Villa, though, swiftly responded as Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to keep out Jackson’s low shot on the hour mark. “A fantastic day to share with our supporters in Villa Park,” said Emery. “We felt that this is our fortress and the energy the supporters gave us was really fantastic.” – Arsenal’s set-piece prowess – Arsenal took advantage to move alongside City on 21 points from eight games with a routine 2-0 win against Everton. Shorn of the creative inspiration of Bukayo Saka, who is set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a thigh injury, Arsenal had to rely on their set-piece prowess to get the job done. Ezri Konsa bundled in his first goal for the club after Everton failed to clear a corner to open the scoring on seven minutes. Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the lead for Mikel Arteta’s men midway through the second period. Fulham further eased the pressure on manager Alvaro Arbeloa with a 1-0 win at Coventry thanks to Oscar Bobb’s individual effort. A second consecutive victory propels the Cottagers out of the relegation zone and up to 12th. Tottenham are also seeking to escape the bottom three when they travel to Chelsea in the evening kick-off, aiming to improve on a terrible record at Stamford Bridge. On Sunday the focus turns on Manchester United boss Michael Carrick when his side take on Bournemouth. A seven-game winless streak has plunged Carrick’s future into doubt just months after he was hired on a two-year deal after a successful interim spell in charge at the end of last season. The stakeholders, speaking at the first anniversary of Circle Mom Fertility Foundation in Abuja, warned that regulatory gaps in in-vitro fertilisation (IVF), surrogacy and other assisted reproductive procedures leave patients, surrogate mothers, donors and children vulnerable to potential abuses. They called for enforceable laws, stronger professional standards, affordable treatment and specialised fertility counselling, while the foundation announced plans to offer 10 free IVF treatment slots to deserving families. Dr Joseph Haruna Kigbu, a medical practitioner and former member of the House of Representatives, warned that Nigeria could no longer rely on general healthcare laws and private agreements to regulate the increasingly complex fertility industry. Kigbu, who previously sponsored a bill seeking to establish a regulatory authority for assisted conception, said the proposal encountered resistance during a public hearing, partly from some practitioners and religious groups. He argued that ethical and religious concerns should not prevent the country from establishing safeguards for patients and children. “Assisted conception is a very complex science. We need specific laws- specific laws that can be enforced when we have erring doctors,” he said. The former lawmaker raised concerns about the possible exploitation of financially vulnerable women involved in egg donation, the handling of donated eggs and embryos, the number of embryos transferred during IVF, disclosure of genetic parentage and the fate of embryos not selected for transfer. Kigbu cited the United Kingdom’s Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority as a regulatory model Nigeria could study, urging lawmakers to establish clear rights and responsibilities for intended parents, surrogate mothers, donors, healthcare providers and children. Babayemi Olaniyan, lead partner at Lehi Attorneys, said Nigeria’s existing legal framework provides some protection for people undergoing assisted reproductive procedures but lacks comprehensive legislation specifically regulating the sector. Olaniyan identified the Constitution, Child Rights Act, Violence Against Persons legislation, National Health Act 2014, medical ethics rules, immigration laws and relevant data-protection provisions as instruments with implications for assisted reproduction. However, he said these laws largely provide general protections rather than detailed regulations covering IVF, intracytoplasmic sperm injection, gamete and embryo donation, fertility preservation and surrogacy. The lawyer stressed that informed consent, confidentiality, parental rights, children’s identities and the responsibilities of medical facilities required clear safeguards. He said properly drafted agreements and independent legal advice were important but could not replace comprehensive legislation. Olaniyan urged fertility practitioners to explain treatment options, risks and implications adequately, avoid promising outcomes that medical science could not guarantee, and ensure children conceived through assisted reproduction were not discriminated against because of their birth circumstances. Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Healthcare Services, Amos Gwamna Magaji, said the National Assembly was working towards addressing regulatory gaps in surrogacy and assisted reproductive procedures. Magaji disclosed that proposed legislation establishing a Nigerian Surrogacy Regulatory Commission had passed second reading in the House in October 2024, with further work required to strengthen the proposed framework. He said the legislation was intended to provide oversight for surrogacy arrangements and protect surrogate mothers, intended parents and children through provisions addressing informed consent, legal parentage, exploitation, medical supervision and accountability for fertility clinics. Acknowledging that religious and cultural objections had complicated previous attempts to regulate assisted reproduction, Magaji urged Nigerians to show greater understanding towards families struggling with infertility. He also advocated stronger health insurance coverage and sustainable financing to reduce treatment costs for low-income families. Founder of Circle Mom Fertility Foundation, Dr Charles Ojeabuo, said the organisation was established to ensure financial hardship did not permanently deny couples the opportunity to become parents. Ojeabuo said the foundation’s mission rested on three pillars: awareness, access and action. He disclosed that it had conducted 8,500 free fertility consultations and registrations during its first year while providing discounted treatment to families. The foundation, he said, was offering 10 free IVF slots, although more than 150 families had applied for assistance. “We will ensure that people will not have to choose between financial limitations and their dream of parenthood,” he said. Citing the World Health Organisation’s estimate that approximately one in six people worldwide experience infertility during their lifetime, Ojeabuo said many couples endure repeated treatment failures, mounting expenses and intense social pressure without adequate emotional or financial support. He disclosed that the foundation also runs a programme known as Mothers and Fathers of Faith, which provides emotional and spiritual encouragement to couples undergoing fertility treatment. He appealed to government agencies, employers, philanthropists and corporate organisations to support fertility care through funding, public education and patient-protection policies. Ojeabuo further advocated livelihood and empowerment support for women whose careers and financial stability were affected by prolonged fertility treatment, stressing the need for a more comprehensive support system for affected families. item.title: Shun partisan politics, Aiyedatiwa tells Ondo corps members
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has charged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) deployed to the state to avoid partisan politics in their host communities. Aiyedatiwa gave the charge at the closing ceremony and terminal parade of the 2026 Batch C Stream I orientation course held at Ikare-Akoko. Represented by the State Coordinator of the scheme, Mrs Kuburat Omowumi Bakare, the governor urged the corps members to be conscious of their responsibilities. “Remain mindful of the responsibilities that come with your position as corps members. Your actions will reflect not only on you but also on your families, your institutions and the NYSC,” he said. He appealed to employers and heads of establishments to receive corps members posted to them with cooperation and understanding. “Provide them with a conducive working environment, appropriate guidance and opportunities to contribute their knowledge and skills. Your mentorship can help them grow professionally and gain valuable experience that will serve them well beyond their service year,” Aiyedatiwa said. He also called on local government authorities, traditional rulers and community leaders to support corps members in their areas to aid their integration and effective execution of Community Development Service projects. “Your cooperation is essential to their successful integration into host communities and to the effective implementation of Community Development Service projects. By working together, we can ensure that the presence of corps members translates into tangible benefits for the people of Ondo State,” he added. The governor further urged the corps members to accept their postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for their host communities. “Approach your responsibilities with a strong sense of duty. Accept your postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for the people among whom you will live and work. He said; “Africa has come to this conversation with great assets, substantial opportunities and a determination to shape its own development based on partnership with the rest of the world. “Foreign capital can only complement but cannot replace the kind of resources that we need,” he said. On Nigeria’s foreign policy, Enikanolaiye said the country was pursuing strategic autonomy, which allows it to engage with different global powers based on its national interests rather than their ideological or political differences. He explained that government had a responsibility to create an enabling environment for private businesses to grow, citing Nigeria’s peacekeeping role in Liberia and Sierra Leone through the Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group, which helped create conditions for Nigerian businesses, including banks, to expand across the region. On mineral resources, the minister called for a shift from exporting raw materials to processing them locally to create jobs and retain more economic value within African countries. He said the Federal Government was requiring investors in the extractive sector to establish local processing industries while strengthening measures to protect the environment and communities where minerals were found. On infrastructure, Enikanolaiye identified reliable electricity, efficient transportation systems and wider digital connectivity as essential to increasing production and supporting economic growth. He said Africa needed sustained investment in these areas to create opportunities for its young population, adding that reliable electricity was also necessary for the continent to benefit from advances in artificial intelligence. The minister identified metering and improved revenue collection in the power sector as additional opportunities for investment. He said African governments had introduced reforms to improve their business environments but stressed that investors needed well-prepared projects, predictable regulations, transparent procurement processes and credible risk-sharing arrangements. Enikanolaiye identified the African Export-Import Bank, African Development Bank and ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development as institutions that could support infrastructure projects through guarantees and blended financing. He also called for reforms to the international credit rating system and welcomed the establishment of an African Credit Rating Agency in Mauritius, saying improved financing arrangements were important to attracting long-term capital. On regional trade, the minister said African countries needed to increase commerce among themselves to strengthen their economies and develop competitive industries. He cited the African Continental Free Trade Area, Nigeria’s single window system and the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System as initiatives that could support trade and economic integration across the continent. He said intra-African trade, which he put at about 16 per cent, needed to increase, while noting that Africa’s average economic growth of 4.3 per cent should rise towards the continent’s ambition of seven per cent. The minister also highlighted the need to review technical education curricula and improve skills development to meet the demands of infrastructure projects. He urged African countries to make better use of diaspora remittances amid declining official development assistance, while reaffirming Nigeria’s commitment to fiscal discipline, transparency, democracy and the rule of law. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s delegation to the dialogue held bilateral engagements in Berlin on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. The delegation was led by Enikanolaiye and the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Atiku Bagudu. On the sidelines of the event, Enikanolaiye and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Germany, Senator Ita Enang, met with Lesotho’s Foreign Minister, Limpho Justice Tau, to discuss ways to strengthen relations between both countries. The meeting also explored the possibility of Lesotho establishing a physical diplomatic presence in Abuja. Tau commended Nigeria’s historical role in the liberation of African countries and invited Nigerian industrialists, including the Dangote Group, to explore investment opportunities in Lesotho. The statement said the meeting was expected to advance cooperation through the African Union Development Agency New Partnership for Africa’s Development. item.title: Tinubu, Shettima flag off APC 2027 campaign in Kaduna
item.description: President Bola Tinubu arrived in Kaduna State on Saturday ahead of the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress’ 2027 presidential campaign, with Vice President Kashim Shettima and his wife, Nana, also arriving for the event. APC National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, the Director-General of the presidential campaign, Abdul’aziz Yari, and Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani were at the airport to welcome the President. Shettima’s arrival was announced in a statement by his spokesman, Stanley Nkwocha. Mr Nkwocha said APC governors, party leaders, elected officials, political stakeholders and supporters were gathering at the Kaduna Township Stadium for the commencement of the party’s nationwide presidential campaign. He described the event as a significant moment for Kaduna, noting that the city would serve as the launching point for the APC’s campaign ahead of the 2027 presidential election. According to the statement, the campaign would provide the ruling party with an opportunity to present its “Renewed Hope 2.0” agenda and highlight the achievements of the Tinubu administration. “The stage is set. Kaduna is ready. The 2027 campaign begins!” the statement read in part. It added, “Asiwaju is here. Northwest for the takeaway!” Ahead of the President’s arrival, security operatives on Saturday barricaded strategic locations across Kaduna metropolis as authorities stepped up security preparations for the campaign event. Personnel from the Nigerian Army, Department of State Services, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Nigeria Immigration Service and the Kaduna State Vigilance Service were deployed to different parts of the city. The security personnel were stationed at major roundabouts and along roads leading to the venue of the campaign flag-off. Muhammadu Buhari Way, formerly known as WAFF Road, was blocked by security operatives ahead of the expected movement of the President and his entourage through the route. The Ahmadu Bello Stadium roundabout was also manned by heavily armed soldiers, police officers and plain-clothes security personnel. The security restrictions affected traffic in several parts of Kaduna, triggering a gridlock that extended from Junction Road to Ahmadu Bello Way. item.title: Thousands March In France Against Far-Right Party Congress
item.description: Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched in the French city of Orléans Saturday against a congress by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) party there, AFP journalists saw. The protest — held on a day of fresh nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living after ones a week ago that devolved into street violence — criticised both Le Pen and centrist President Emmanuel Macron. France’s President Emmanuel Macron meets with elected officials at the town hall following a shooting in Trappes, near Paris, on October 23, 2026. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled, while carrying placards that read “The Youth say ‘screw you’ to the National Rally” and “Hotter than fascists”. The two-day RN congress in Orleans was the first big party campaign rally by Le Pen, whom surveys put as the leading candidate to succeed Macron in presidential elections in six months.
